lastCompletedStory.title: Add per-attempt content recompute to the CAS commit-tree writers

nextStoryContext: commitTreeToMain's `files` param and writeIssueFile's `extraFiles` option now accept EITHER a static FileWrite[] (unchanged) OR a FileWritesFn callback `(mainSha: string) => FileWrite[]`, invoked once per CAS attempt (after read-tree establishes that attempt's fresh main sha, exported from src/git/on-main.ts). writeIssueFile resolves it via the new private helper `resolveExtraFiles(extraFiles, currentMainSha)` in src/issues/alloc.ts. All existing callers (issue-specify.ts, journal.ts, triage.ts, suggestions.ts, domain-docs.ts, journal-archive.ts, patterns-archive.ts, createLocalIssueOnMain) pass a static FileWrite[]/array and are behaviour-unchanged (typeof check short-circuits to the array branch). This story only added the primitive; per the PRD note, US-002 is expected to route an actual pen/whole-file-overwrite writer (likely promoteSuggestionOnMain or similar) through the callback form to fix the real concurrent-clobber bug -- check prd.json for the exact US-002 scope before assuming which caller. Gotcha hit this story: biome's noExcessiveLinesPerFunction (max 80 lines/function, no per-file override exists for alloc.ts) tripped when the recompute logic was inlined into writeIssueFile; fixed by extracting the one-line typeof-branch into a private `resolveExtraFiles` helper -- if a future story adds more inline logic to writeIssueFile or commitTreeToMain, watch this ceiling before assuming a biome override is needed.
